kjv_text: My strength is dried up like a potsherd; and my tongue cleaveth to my jaws; and thou hast brought me into the dust of death. ... I thirst.

thread.thread: Psalm 22:15 paints the killing thirst of a dying man -- strength dried up like a potsherd, tongue cleaving to the jaws, sinking into the dust of death -- written in the first person by David about someone else's death, about 1000 years before Jesus cried 'I thirst' on the cross (John 19:28). This is a DESCRIPTIVE match -- the psalm pictures the thirst behind that cry, it does NOT foretell or cite it (John 19:28's fulfilment formula is referred to Psalm 69:21, which is never quoted here). The gospel turn: the One who made every river and offers the world living water hung there with nothing, thirsting in your place, so you could drink and never thirst again -- and that water is Himself.
thread.lever: overlooked detail / descriptive match (Ps 22:15 paints the dying man's killing thirst, a thousand years early; NOT a cited verbal fulfilment -- the Ps 69:21 landmine is guarded, John's 'that the scripture might be fulfilled' clause is never quoted)
thread.anchor_detail: the dying man's body giving out from thirst -- strength dried like a potsherd, tongue stuck fast to the jaws, sinking into the dust of death -- the picture Jesus then lived when He cried 'I thirst'
thread.why_fresh: the Giver of living water, who made every ocean, cried out in thirst -- and Psalm 22 had painted that exact dying thirst a thousand years before Rome's cross
thread.gospel_landing: the One who offers living water went dry in your place so you could drink and never thirst again; that water is Himself; come to Him and drink
thread.rationale: v15 (the thirst / dust of death) framed as an honest descriptive match -- the psalm paints the thirst, it does not cite the cry (Ps 69 landmine guarded) -- with a grace landing (He went dry in your place); distinct from short #7 (the body, v14/17) with no overlap of quoted spans

beats.text: The One who made every ocean gasped two words on a cross: I thirst.

Psalm twenty-two. David wrote it in the first person, but he was picturing someone else's death. Watch the body give out: "My strength is dried up like a potsherd; and my tongue cleaveth to my jaws; and thou hast brought me into the dust of death."

Dried clay; a tongue stuck fast; a man sinking into the dust of death. Then John records the dying Jesus' cry: "I thirst." Psalm twenty-two doesn't foretell that cry — it paints the thirst behind it, a thousand years before He felt it.
And think who is thirsting: the One who made every river and spring, who offers the world living water — hanging there with nothing, in your place.
He went dry so that you could drink and never thirst again. The God who made every ocean cried out in thirst — so He could hand you the one water that never fails. And that water is Himself.
